sessions.phase_label: Front-end Release 1 audit scoping and assessment
Audit delivery and Connector Module refocus

requirements.title: Front-End Release 1 Audit
requirements.definition: Produce a written assessment of sufficiently built Release 1 front-end routes and screens, including a readiness recommendation, prioritised evidence-backed findings, relevant risks, remediation estimates, and explicit assumptions and exclusions.
requirements.boundary_note: The requested recommendation, findings, risk analysis, remediation estimates, evidence references, and written format are acceptance attributes of one audit artifact. The later Connector Module request changes the artifact's scope and packaging rather than establishing a separate assessment mechanism.

requirements.title: Account Member List
requirements.definition: Allow an account owner to retrieve and view the members associated with the account.
requirements.boundary_note: Member listing has its own expected output and backend capability and can be implemented or fail independently of invitation acceptance and member mutation actions.

requirements.title: Account Member Access Revocation
requirements.definition: Allow an account owner to revoke an existing member's access through a supported account-management action.
requirements.boundary_note: This concerns revoking a team member's account access. It is distinct from removing the member and from disconnecting an external connector integration.

requirements.title: Account Member Removal
requirements.definition: Allow an account owner to remove a member from the account through a supported member-management action.
requirements.boundary_note: Removal is retained separately from access revocation because the source identifies them as distinct actions and they may require different semantics and endpoints.

requirements.title: Owner-Facing Member Usage Metering
requirements.definition: Provide account owners with per-member token-consumption information and a usage breakdown rather than limiting that information to the superadmin console.
requirements.boundary_note: Usage visibility is independently testable from the ability to configure individual member limits. Whether the owner-facing capability belongs in Release 1 or Phase 2 is unresolved in the supplied history.

requirements.title: Owner-Facing Member Usage Limits
requirements.definition: Provide account owners with access to individual usage-limit controls or information for each account member.
requirements.boundary_note: Individual limits can be implemented, modified, and verified independently of displaying per-member consumption. Release-phase placement remains unresolved because the client response occurred outside the supplied messages.

requirements.title: Member Invitation Acceptance Submission
requirements.definition: Provide an end-to-end flow in which an invited account member can follow an invitation link, reach an appropriate route, and have the invitation accepted by the system.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers invitation landing and acceptance as one end-to-end mechanism. Member listing, revocation, and removal are separate owner actions with independently implementable endpoints.

requirements.title: Persisted Connector Access Revocation
requirements.definition: When a connector or external connection is disconnected, remove its persisted connection record immediately and report success only when revocation actually occurred.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a connector-disconnection behavior with its own persistence and success-reporting criteria, not the team-member revocation action.

unresolved_candidates.description: The client's detailed Slack responses are absent. Multi-user and instant-revocation scope are summarized later, but the exact Release 1 status of member-list, member-revocation, member-removal, owner-facing metering, and individual-limit capabilities cannot be fully established.
Wallet is named as part of client-confirmed scope, but the supplied evidence does not define the expected Wallet behavior well enough to establish a Requirement boundary.

The client requests exclusive focus on the Connector Module and a separate presentation, but the text contains an unclear suffix and does not enumerate the precise Connector Module routes or findings included.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I’d like you to assess the front end and give me your recommendation for release 1.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001], that is reasonable. I’ll send you the list of R1 routes and screens that are built sufficiently for assessment.
After the Upwork contract and the confidentiality/IP arrangements have been completed, we’ll grant named, read-only repo access and provide a staging URL. This will exclude production credentials and customer data.
Before granting access, please confirm that your proposed review deliverable will cover:
a Release 1 readiness recommendation
prioritised blockers and findings supported by evidence
risks relating to security, architecture, performance and maintainability
recommended remediation with indicative effort
clearly stated assumptions and anything excluded from the review
For now, please also give me either an indicative price range or a capped discovery allowance. Once you have examined the materials, you can confirm the final scope, fixed price and delivery date.

value_updates.review_scope: Release 1 routes and screens identified as sufficiently built for assessment
value_updates.findings: prioritised blockers and findings supported by evidence

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Okay, great—I’m comfortable proceeding on that basis. Please send me a proposal through upowork, and we can take it from there.

value_updates.evidence_citation_format: Every finding identifies the relevant file and line

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
The front-end Release 1 audit has now been completed. All materials are available in the shared Drive folder at [URL_001]:

• BIQc Audit — Word — the seven-document report
• BIQc Audit — Markdown source — identical content prepared for Anjali
• working journal — the verification task list provided for reference

Please begin with 01\_FOUNDER\_SUMMARY. It is designed for a reader without a technical background and explains the recommendation, readiness by module, and cost. The remaining files provide supporting detail: 02 contains the complete findings register with file/line evidence and hours; 03 gives the remediation sequence; 04 is the evidence log; 05 addresses the scope and timeline question; and 06 states the assumptions and exclusions.

The headline conclusion is that I cannot recommend approving Release 1 for an external launch in its present condition. In addition, the scope you confirmed on Sunday—multi-user, instant revocation, Wallet—cannot fit within this week. Section 6 of the founder summary describes two viable paths forward.

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports completing and delivering the front-end Release 1 audit with its recommendation, findings register, file-and-line evidence, remediation sequence, evidence log, and assumptions and exclusions.

Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], I’m following up regarding the files delivered on Tuesday: the corrected report pack and complete evidence bundle, covering every item you requested.

All contracted work has been completed, and I have no remaining outstanding items. When you have a moment, could you please close the milestone?

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], I have three scope questions arising from the front-end review. These are product decisions rather than defects, so they need your input rather than Anjali’s.

1. Does the multi-user scenario belong in Release 1? The functionality for sending an invite exists, but the front end does not call POST /account/users/accept, and there is no route for the invitation link, leaving invited users with nowhere to land. Completing the flow end-to-end would also require backend functionality for the member-list, revoke and remove actions, and none of those endpoints currently exist.

2. The product description promises "Instant access revocation", but while #1427 remains open, the disconnect endpoints report success without deleting the connection record. The front end handles this properly by refusing to report success, which means the current behaviour does not match the claim.

3. Anjali’s requirements for per-member metering—token consumption per member, usage breakdown and individual limits—are available only in the superadmin console under /admin. Account owners cannot access any of these features. Was an owner-facing view intended for R1, or does it belong to Phase 2?

ambiguity.description: It is unresolved whether account-member listing, as part of the multi-user scenario, belongs in Release 1 scope.
